html:
The Battle of Pylos was fought on land and sea in 425 BCE at Pylos, on the Bay of Navarino in the southwest Peloponnese. It was one of the biggest Athenian successes of the Peloponnesian War.

A storm drove an Athenian fleet ashore at Pylos, and the general Demosthenes had the soldiers fortify the headland. This was a base inside Sparta's own territory, close to the helots Sparta depended on. The Spartans attacked and landed several hundred soldiers on the island of Sphacteria across the bay. Then the Athenian fleet returned, beat the Spartan ships, and cut the men on the island off.

Sparta offered peace to get them back. Athens, led by Cleon, refused. Cleon and Demosthenes then stormed the island with light troops and archers. Nearly three hundred men surrendered, about 120 of them full Spartan citizens. Greeks had believed Spartans would always die rather than give up, so the surrender stunned them.

Athens held the prisoners as hostages, which kept Spartan armies out of Attica. They were handed back under the Peace of Nicias in 421 BCE.
